about: Dispatch Planning (shared/PRODUCTION_FLOWS.md has no entry for this yet - it postdates that doc). How much of an order line's rolls/belts remains to be dispatched, and whether a line counts as fully dispatched. Both apps read this file in their tests. The write only happens dashboard-side (client/); the app side only ever reads this to show a rep or manager 'X of Y dispatched'.

fields.note: custom_rolls/custom_loose_belts are what was ordered. custom_dispatched_rolls/custom_dispatched_loose_belts are cumulative across every Manna Dispatch that has ever touched this line - never a single dispatch's own amount.

remaining.why: never dispatched at all: the full ordered quantity remains
the case the feature exists for: 9 of 10 went out, 1 remains - visible as a shortfall, not silently dropped
a belts-only line (PCTR sold in loose belts, not whole rolls) tracks its own remainder independently of rolls
a rolls-only line (CTR, bonding gum, solution - belts never apply) reads belts as flatly zero on both sides

Frappe's three spellings of an unset Int read as the same zero, matching the rule production_order.json already pins for Data fields - a line that has genuinely never had a dispatch written to it must not look over-dispatched
the string 'null' from naive interpolation reads as unset too, not as a literal value

over-dispatch is a data mistake, not a valid state - cumulative recorded greater than ordered clamps to zero remaining rather than going negative, the opposite rounding direction from production.ts's 'errors round down': under-reporting what already left the building is the more dangerous failure here, so this rounds the other way on purpose

fully_dispatched.why: nothing dispatched yet is not fully dispatched
partially dispatched is not fully dispatched - this is the flag that keeps a line reappearing in Dispatch Planning across rounds
rolls and belts both fully out means the line is done
rolls done but belts still owed is not fully dispatched - the two counters do not average out

an over-dispatched line (data mistake) reads as fully dispatched rather than blocking forever on a number that can never be reached exactly - once dispatched-so-far meets or exceeds ordered, the line is gone, full stop
a line with nothing ordered at all (both zero) has nothing outstanding and is vacuously fully dispatched
